country.name: Palestine
country.tagline: Monastic and family wineries in the West Bank keeping Hebron's ancient grapes alive.

stats.note: Very small production from a handful of wineries; no official statistics found.

country.overview:
The hills of Hebron and Bethlehem have grown grapes since antiquity, and Palestinian farmers kept local varieties alive as table grapes and raisins through centuries when wine was not made commercially. Today a few wineries operate in the West Bank. The Salesian monastery of Cremisan, on the edge of Beit Jala near Bethlehem, has made wine since 1885 and bottles single-variety wines from the ancient local grapes Hamdani, Jandali, Dabouki and Baladi, sourced from Palestinian growers around Hebron. In the Christian village of Taybeh, north-east of Ramallah, the Khoury family, known for Palestine's first craft brewery (1994), opened Taybeh Winery in 2013.

Winemaking here is shaped by occupation: checkpoints, permits and the separation barrier affect access to vineyards and markets. The Cremisan valley itself has been the subject of a long legal and political dispute over the barrier's route through monastery and village land.

history.title: Cremisan's monks begin making wine
history.text: Italian Salesian monks set up a winery at the Cremisan monastery near Beit Jala.

history.title: Ancient grapes bottled
history.text: With Italian oenologist Riccardo Cotarella's advice, Cremisan began releasing varietal Hamdani, Jandali, Dabouki and Baladi.

history.title: Taybeh Winery opens
history.text: The Khoury family added a winery to their Taybeh brewery in the Christian village north-east of Ramallah.

country.climate_soils: Mediterranean hill climate at 700 to 1,000 metres around Hebron and Bethlehem; limestone and terra rossa; dry farming of old bush vines is common.

grapes.name: Hamdani and Jandali
grapes.note: Ancient whites from the Hebron hills, often blended.

grapes.name: Dabouki
grapes.note: White grape thought to be among the oldest local varieties.

sites.name: Cremisan Monastery winery
sites.text: The Salesian monastery on a terraced hillside between Beit Jala and Jerusalem has made wine since 1885 and now bottles the ancient Palestinian grapes Hamdani, Jandali, Dabouki and Baladi bought from Hebron-area growers.

sites.name: Taybeh Winery
sites.text: The Khoury family's winery, opened in 2013 next to their brewery in the Christian village of Taybeh, north-east of Ramallah.
